papers.title: Consistent and idiosyncratic pleiotropy in shaping genetic correlations.
papers.summary: Develops a bivariate marker-effect framework for recombinant mapping populations that separates large-effect covariance contributors from the polygenic background correlation (rd). Applying it to yeast single-cell morphology shows trait pairs with similar genetic correlations (rg) can differ sharply in rd, and stronger rd predicts greater environmental stability of rg under HSP90 perturbation.

papers.title: Acetate suppresses tumorigenesis through ACSS2-dependent H2A.Z acetylation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.summary: Acetate levels and ACSS2 are decreased in human esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), with low ACSS2 linked to poor prognosis. Exogenous acetate inhibits ESCC proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, ACSS2 promotes H2A.Z acetylation that transcriptionally activates ACSS2 itself and ATM, defining an acetate-ACSS2-H2A.Zac-ATM tumor-suppressive axis.

papers.title: 16S ribosomal RNA modification drives transcript-specific translation efficiency.
papers.summary: Deletion of mraW (RsmH), a 16S rRNA methyltransferase, corrects a late-stage sporulation defect in Bacillus subtilis by bypassing a checkpoint. Ribosomes from ΔmraW cells show ~2-fold lower translation efficiency and reduced production of checkpoint protein CmpA via a stem-loop in its mRNA. mraW modification enhances general translation efficiency.

papers.title: Emergent 3D genome reorganization and graded gene control from the stepwise assembly of transcriptional condensates.
papers.summary: Shows transcriptional condensates assemble stepwise in the yeast heat shock response: Hsf1 clusters first, Mediator partitions next, then Pol II condenses, driving coalescence of heat-shock genes. Separation-of-function mutants reveal graded (non-switch-like) gene control and decoupling of condensate formation from activation, with fully assembled condensates promoting adaptive 3D genome reconfiguration.

papers.title: A novel curcumin analog sAc15 alleviates LPS-induced acute lung injury by activating the PI3K/AKT/Nrf2 pathway in pulmonary epithelial cells.
papers.journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
papers.summary: Evaluates sAc15, a stable curcumin analog, in LPS-induced acute lung injury. sAc15 shows broader safety margins and superior ROS suppression versus curcumin, binds Nrf2 directly (Kd 2.68 µM), and mitigates pulmonary inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Effects are mediated by PI3K/AKT activation and Nrf2/HO-1/NQO-1 upregulation, highlighting a therapeutic candidate for ALI/ARDS.

papers.title: Ribosome heterogeneity provides a translational barrier against protein misfolding disease in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: Identifies Rpl24b, a 60S ribosomal protein, as a key anti-prion factor in yeast. Deleting rpl24b increases [PSI+] prion generation frequency and yields stable, high-propagon variants. Val138 in Rpl24b is the major determinant; loss of Rpl24b perturbs protein quality control and accumulates misfolded aggregates, providing a translational barrier against protein misfolding disease.

papers.title: The Histidine 382 Residue Influences the Thermal Stability and Binding Propensity of the E2 Domain of Amyloid Precursor Protein.
papers.summary: Reinvestigates how the ΔH382L missense mutation affects the E2 domain of amyloid precursor protein. The mutation reduces thermal stability (Tm −10.1°C), reverses Cu2+-mediated stabilization, and weakens heparin binding. Molecular dynamics simulations link it to increased rigidity in one helical subdomain, altered native contacts, and rerouted communication pathways.

papers.title: The evolutionary maintenance of amino acid prototrophy in Escherichia coli.
papers.summary: Tests evolutionary robustness of amino acid prototrophy in E. coli. Spontaneous suppressor mutations could rescue only 10 of 59 irreversible auxotrophy-causing mutations (detection limit ~7e-11). Findings argue metabolic rewiring alone is insufficient and that horizontal gene transfer of housekeeping genes is critical to counteract mutational degradation (Muller's ratchet).

papers.title: The anterior subcutaneous WAT has greater beiging potential than the inguinal WAT in mice.
papers.summary: Compares beiging potential of anterior subcutaneous (asWAT) versus inguinal (iWAT) white adipose depots in mice under thermoneutral and cold conditions. asWAT shows a more pronounced beige-like phenotype: smaller adipocytes, higher thermogenic gene expression, and greater mitochondrial abundance/activity, with enrichment of thermogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation pathways.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory and protective effects of Aloe vera on intestinal function in zebrafish.
papers.summary: Evaluates Aloe vera gel (Aloe-S0) and its polysaccharide-rich fraction (APS-CPIC) in a TNBS-induced zebrafish model of intestinal inflammation. Both reduce inflammation and mucosal damage, increase goblet cells, restore the mucus barrier, and improve motility, downregulating pro-inflammatory genes (prkcq, sfmbt1, tyk2) and upregulating jag2b, supporting therapeutic potential for IBD.

papers.title: Enhanced mitigation of diabetic myocardial injury in rats via modulating the adiponectin/IRS-1/PI3K/p-AKT/FOXO-1 signaling by combining methotrexate and insulin.
papers.summary: Combines low-dose methotrexate (MTX) and insulin (Ins) in a rat model of diabetic myocardial injury. The combination more effectively improves cardiac injury biomarkers, lipid profile, histopathology, and suppresses oxidative stress and apoptosis. MTX enhances insulin's stimulatory effect on the adiponectin/IRS-1/PI3K/p-AKT/FOXO-1 pathway in the heart.

papers.title: Staphylococcus aureus biofilms: molecular mechanisms, resistance determinants, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: Comprehensive review of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation: genetic regulators, resistance determinants, host-biofilm and polymicrobial interactions. Highlights complementary resistance mechanisms (limited antimicrobial penetration, persister cells, adaptive stress responses) and emerging strategies including matrix-disrupting agents, quorum-sensing inhibitors, antimicrobial peptides, phages, nanotech delivery, CRISPR-Cas therapeutics, and combination therapy.

papers.title: Development of endothelial injury under chemical hypoxia: early migration impairment precedes cytotoxicity in CoCl(2)-treated EA.hy926 cells.
papers.summary: Establishes a standardized CoCl2-induced endothelial dysfunction model in EA.hy926 cells and characterizes temporal progression. Migration impairment is the earliest detectable defect (12 h, before significant apoptosis), followed by early apoptosis at 24 h and late apoptosis/secondary necrosis at 48 h. Progressive Hif-1α downregulation with Phd2 upregulation indicates negative-feedback regulation under severe chemical hypoxia.

papers.title: Exosome in Hashimoto's thyroiditis: from pathogenesis to diagnostic and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: Reviews the role of exosomes in Hashimoto's thyroiditis pathogenesis. Exosomal Hsp60 cross-reacts with TPO/Tg, T-cell exosomes carrying miR-142-3p impair regulatory T cells, and patient-derived exosomes activate dendritic cells via TLR2/3-NF-κB to drive Th1/Th17 polarization. Discusses exosomal signatures as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies including exosome-release inhibitors and engineered MSC-derived exosomes.

papers.title: Autophagy-associated exosomal microRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer: a discovery-phase study.
papers.summary: Discovery-phase study examining exosomal microRNA remodeling in triple-negative breast cancer under doxorubicin-induced autophagy. Small RNA sequencing identified 17 differentially expressed exomiRs, with hsa-miR-1468-5p confirmed in MDA-MB-231 (23.97-fold). In-silico targets converge on BECN1 and autophagy/apoptosis nodes. Authors note the data do not establish causality between autophagy and cargo changes; validation was limited.

papers.title: Apigenin Alleviates Ligamentum Flavum Ossification by Dual-Targeting CA9 and CDK6 and Modulating Calcium/PI3K-Akt Signaling.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.summary: Uses network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking to examine apigenin in ligamentum flavum ossification (OLF). Identifies dual targeting of CA9 and CDK6 with modulation of calcium and PI3K-AKT signaling. Docking shows binding energies below −5 kcal/mol, and molecular dynamics support stability of apigenin-target complexes, offering initial therapeutic insights.

papers.title: Serum Metabolomics and Multiomics Validation Reveal Zishangan Granule-Induced P53-Bax/Casp3 Signaling in NSCLC.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.summary: Investigates Zishangan granule (ZSG), a four-herb formulation, against non-small cell lung cancer using serum metabolomics, network pharmacology, and an LLC mouse model. ZSG reduces tumor weight by 58.3% and increases tumor-cell apoptosis ~3-fold, upregulating p53, p21, Bax, Casp3, PTEN and PARP1, supporting P53-associated Bax/Casp3 apoptotic signaling.

papers.title: ABCC6 in Cellular Metabolic Homeostasis: Biochemical Links to Extracellular Nucleotide Signaling, Mitochondrial Stress, and Senescence.
papers.summary: Review of ABCC6, a liver-enriched transporter. Beyond pseudoxanthoma elasticum, it promotes hepatocyte ATP/ADP release and ENPP1-dependent pyrophosphate generation, maintaining anti-mineralization buffering. ABCC6 deficiency is associated with altered lipoprotein metabolism, mitochondrial bioenergetic impairment, oxidative stress, and senescence-like phenotypes. Discusses therapeutic strategies restoring PPi availability or ABCC6 function.

papers.title: In vivo and In Silico Assessment of Acampe papillosa (Lindl.) Lindl. Seed Extract: A Multi-Pharmacological Approach.
papers.summary: Assesses the methanolic extract of Acampe papillosa seeds (ME-APS) in mice with in silico support. GC-MS identified 13 bioactive compounds. The extract showed dose-dependent antipyretic and central analgesic activity, peripheral analgesic and antidepressant-like effects, and moderate anxiolytic response. Molecular docking and ADMET predictions supported favorable interactions and low toxicity risk.

papers.title: Host-Derived Proteomic Profiling of Human and Canine Mammary Tumor Xenografts Identifies Enrichment of Lipid Metabolism-Related Pathways.
papers.summary: Comparative proteomic profiling of host-derived proteins in human (MDA-MB-231) and canine (CMT-U27) mammary tumor xenografts. 577 proteins were differentially expressed in tumor versus healthy mammary tissue. Lipid metabolism-related pathways were altered with moderate concordance between species, suggesting lipid pathways may contribute to tumor-associated microenvironmental changes; findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: METTL3-Mediated m6A Modification of ACTR2 Promotes Trophoblast Cell Growth, Migration and Invasion in Unexplained Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion.
papers.summary: Shows ACTR2 is downregulated in unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion and promotes trophoblast (HTR-8/SVneo) growth, migration, and invasion. METTL3 enhances m6A modification of ACTR2 recognized by YTHDF2, reducing ACTR2 mRNA stability. METTL3 knockdown activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, suggesting METTL3-mediated ACTR2 m6A as a novel therapeutic target.

papers.title: A Novel Constitutional TUBB Variant Associated With Familial Malformations of Cortical Development.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: Reports father-to-daughter transmission of a novel constitutional TUBB variant (c.991C>T; p.Leu331Phe) associated with intellectual disability and malformations of cortical development. Functional assays in patient fibroblasts showed impaired cell motility, altered cytoskeleton organization, and changed cellular morphology, indicating that pathogenic germline TUBB variants can occasionally be inherited given a relatively mild phenotype.

papers.title: Inversion-driven mitochondrial gene rearrangements and their evolutionary implications in Littorinimorpha: insights from the Eunaticina papilla mitogenome.
papers.summary: Sequences and analyzes the complete mitogenome of Eunaticina papilla (16,415 bp, 37 genes). Comparative analysis reveals extensive inversion-driven gene rearrangements (3 clusters spanning 15 tRNAs and 8 PCGs). Phylogenetic analyses support monophyly of Littorinimorpha, place E. papilla within Naticidae, and refine relationships with Polinices and Mammilla.
